extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and preparation of patent specifications covering incorporation by reference, substitute specifications, marks/trade names, prophetic examples, restoration of canceled matter, and related procedural requirements under the MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective incorporation by reference (general compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference must comply with 37 CFR 1.57(c), (d), and (e) to be effective; otherwise it is not effective to incorporate such material unless corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporation is noncompliant the material is not incorporated unless corrected within any Office-set time period and in no case later than the close of prosecution (37 CFR 1.114(b)) or abandonment of the application (37 CFR 1.57(h)). Examiners should make any underlying objection or rejection (e.g., under 35 U.S.C. 112) until the applicant corrects the improper incorporation by reference by submitting an amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.57(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of incorporation by reference (37 CFR 1.57(g) & (h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously noncompliant incorporation by reference statement may be corrected by an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(g), but the amendment must not include new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.57(h)(1) permits correcting omissions of the root words 'incorporate' and 'reference' where the application as filed clearly conveys intent to incorporate. 37 CFR 1.57(h)(2) permits correction of a citation where the document is sufficiently described to uniquely identify it. Corrections that cannot identify the intended document may be new matter and are not authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction timing and limits for incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to noncompliant incorporations must be made within any Office-set time period for the correction and cannot be made later than the close of prosecution or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office first notices noncompliance and informs the applicant, the Office may set a time period for correction; otherwise an applicant noticing noncompliance must inform the Office and correct before the close of prosecution or abandonment (37 CFR 1.57(h)). Petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to suspend this time is not appropriate; other remedies depend on status (revive under 1.137 for abandoned apps, reissue after issuance).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment used to correct an improper incorporation by reference must not introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated by reference and that the amendment contains no new matter is required (37 CFR 1.57(g)). If correction would alter scope of the claims (e.g., by adding omitted equivalent means), such changes should be made via the reissue process rather than correction under 1.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of filing date upon correction (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application will not be affected by applicant’s correction of an improperly incorporated essential material where certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date remains if (A) clear intent to incorporate existed and correction only adds root words 'incorporate'/'reference'; (B) the incorporated document can be uniquely identified and correction clarifies identification; and (C) correction inserts material from a reference where incorporation is to an unpublished U.S. application, foreign application or patent, or to a publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner response to improper incorporation of essential material
rubrics_metrics.description: If essential material is improperly incorporated by reference, the examiner should object to the specification and/or reject the claim(s) (e.g., under 35 U.S.C. 112) until corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if essential material from a foreign patent was incorporated improperly, examiner may require applicant to amend the specification to include that essential material in reply to a non-final Office action, and applicant must file the amendment and required statement within the reply time. If applicant later adds claim limitations supported only by the foreign patent, examiner may reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and treat the Office action as final; applicant may then use after-final amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 or file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with a 1.57(g) amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference as a safeguard for priority/benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference statement filed at the time of filing a later application may permit inclusion of subject matter from the prior application without it being considered new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To serve as an effective safeguard, the incorporation statement must be filed at time of filing the later application; adding such statement after filing is not effective because no new matter can be added after the filing date (35 U.S.C. 132(a)). An incorporation statement will not substitute for the specific reference requirements of 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 or 37 CFR 1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior applications to establish an earlier effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on incorporations in U.S. applications that issue as patents do not apply where an earlier application is relied upon solely to establish an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 119 or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is entitled to rely upon the filing date of an earlier application even if that earlier application itself incorporates essential material by reference. However, when benefit/priority is claimed, the applicant may be required to supply copies (and translations if necessary) of incorporated material so the Office can determine whether the earlier application disclosed the invention as required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulated/predicted test results and prophetic (paper) examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulated or predicted test results and prophetical (paper) examples are permitted, but they must not be represented as having been actually performed or as actual results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working examples are those actually performed and may describe tests conducted and achieved results. Paper examples describe how to make an embodiment not actually conducted and should not be represented as work actually done; no results should be represented as actual unless achieved. Paper examples should not be described using the past tense (Hoffman‑La Roche v. Promega).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification requirements (37 CFR 1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require the entire specification or part thereof be rewritten if the number/nature of amendments or legibility renders the application difficult to consider or arrange for printing/copying (37 CFR 1.125(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification (excluding claims) may be voluntarily filed up to payment of the issue fee if accompanied by a statement that it includes no new matter (37 CFR 1.125(b)). A substitute filed under 1.125 must be submitted with markings showing all changes relative to the immediate prior version (underline added text; strike-through or double brackets for deleted text) and an accompanying clean version without markings. Substitute specs are not permitted in reissue applications or reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.125(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and marking of substitute specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification submitted under 37 CFR 1.125 must show changes relative to the immediate prior version with specified conventions and include a clean copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added subject matter shown by underlining; deleted matter shown by strike-through or double brackets (for deletions of five or fewer characters or when strike-through is hard to perceive). Paragraph numbering of the specification of record is not considered a change that must be shown. Paragraphs of substitute spec (other than claims) should be individually numbered in Arabic numerals to facilitate replacement paragraphs under 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of substitute specifications and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no obligation on the examiner to perform a detailed comparison to determine whether new matter has been added in a substitute specification, but the examiner should object if aware of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner becomes aware that new matter is present in a voluntarily filed substitute specification, an objection should be made. A substitute spec that complies with 37 CFR 1.125 should normally be entered; one denied entry should be marked as such and applicant notified (form paragraph 6.28.02). Substitute specifications filed after final action or appeal are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; those filed after mailing of a notice of allowance are governed by 37 CFR 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of canceled matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled text in the specification can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously canceled matter as a new insertion (37 CFR 1.121(b)(4)); a canceled claim reinstated only as a new claim with a new claim number (37 CFR 1.121(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is treated as new insertion, so the applicant must present the canceled matter anew as part of the prosecution record. See MPEP § 714 for related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/use of specification or drawings in subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of a specification or drawings can normally be transferred to another application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.02(i) for details; generally material cannot be moved between patent applications so as to avoid new matter issues or chain-of-title/ownership issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of marks and trade names in patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark or trade name may be used in a patent application to identify an article, product, service, or organization only if (A) its meaning is established by an accompanying definition in the specification that is sufficiently descriptive, enabling, precise and definite to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 112, or (B) its meaning is well-known to one skilled in the art and satisfactorily defined in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (A) or (B) must be met at the time of filing. Identification introduced by amendment must be restricted to characteristics known at the time of filing to avoid new matter. If proper identification is omitted and necessary, the examiner should reject claims that merely rely on identification by mark/trade name as insufficient disclosure. Arbitrary marks liable to mean different things do not constitute definite language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for proprietary nature and presentation of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietary nature of marks used in commerce should be respected: marks should be capitalized (or accompanied by ™, SM, ® where appropriate) or otherwise identified so their proprietary nature is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may search TESS to determine registration status and applicable goods. Avoid language that hides the fact a term is a mark (e.g., do not use 'commonly known as' formulations that obscure it). Use of a mark in the title of an application should be avoided; if a registered mark is a symbol/device depicted in a drawing, identify it in the brief or detailed description. If misuse appears in a published application and the application is pending, the Office should ensure the mark is replaced by appropriate generic terminology.
